title: Selfing, Inbreeding, and Inbreeding Depression
objective: Explain how selfing changes genotype frequencies, exposes recessive alleles, increases line uniformity, and can reduce vigor or fertility.
coreScience: Selfing mates a plant with genetically female pollen derived from itself or otherwise allows self-fertilization. Under an ideal diploid single-locus model, heterozygosity is expected to halve with each selfed generation. The genome does not become instantly homozygous, and different regions fix at different times because of recombination, selection, viability, and structural variation.

Inbreeding exposes recessive alleles and can reveal hidden defects in vigor, fertility, development, disease response, sex expression, and seed quality. Inbreeding depression is the decline in performance caused by increased homozygosity for deleterious alleles and loss of favorable heterozygous combinations. Its magnitude differs among populations and traits. Selection can remove some severe defects, but “purging” is not guaranteed and may narrow diversity.

An S1 family is a population of selfed offspring from one parent, not a clone of that parent. It can segregate widely when the parent is heterozygous. Selfing can help reveal genotype, create mapping populations, and develop lines, but it should be paired with population size, family testing, and backup conservation. Do not interpret short-term uniformity in a few plants as genetic stability.
cultivationRelevance: Track selfing generation separately from filial generation, compare each selfed family with the parent and outcrossed checks, and record losses rather than discarding them from the analysis.
measureAndRecord: Before evaluating selfing, inbreeding, and inbreeding depression, record the breeding population, generation, identities, and measurement context, including Parent ID and heterozygosity, selfing method, S generation, seed set and germination. Keep definitions and identifiers stable so ancestry, family, and phenotype records remain comparable across generations.

During evaluation, track family size, vigor, fertility, sex and abnormality rates together with the mating design, environment, developmental stage, replicate or family structure, and any selection event that could alter interpretation. Preserve raw values and rejected or missing cases rather than only the selected outcome.

At the decision point, document trait variance, molecular homozygosity, selected families and preserved backups.. State the evidence supporting advancement, note uncertainty and correlated tradeoffs, and retain enough pedigree and sample traceability to reconstruct the decision later.
misconceptions: S1 seed is genetically identical to the mother. This ignores segregation, environmental effects, sampling error, and the possibility that the observed phenotype does not transmit predictably to progeny.

Selfing always creates a stable line in one generation. A label, generation name, or single phenotype does not establish genetic value by itself; use family, progeny, marker, or replicated performance evidence appropriate to the trait.

Inbreeding depression affects every Cannabis population equally. The claim should not be generalized beyond the tested population, parents, environments, and measurement methods without additional validation.
evidenceLimits: Heterozygosity decline is an expectation; realized fixation and depression depend on starting genotype, selection, linkage, viability, and population size. Expected genetic ratios, breeding values, and response magnitudes are model- and population-dependent, so they should not be presented as guaranteed outcomes for untested parents or environments.

Evidence from markers, pedigrees, replicated phenotypes, progeny tests, and laboratory assays answers different questions. Strong release claims require the relevant evidence type, adequate sample size, traceable methods, and confirmation that the result persists in the target breeding population and environment.

knowledgeCheck: For "Selfing, Inbreeding, and Inbreeding Depression", explain the mechanism behind this objective: Explain how selfing changes genotype frequencies, exposes recessive alleles, increases line uniformity, and can reduce vigor or fertility. Which observation or measurement would best test whether that mechanism is operating in the real crop?

A learner claims, "S1 seed is genetically identical to the mother." Use the lesson's science and evidence limits to explain why that claim is unreliable, then name one observation or measurement that could separate the competing explanations.
